description:
Tetramote turns your phone into a remote for your computer. See its screen, hear its sound, and use it with a trackpad, touch and a keyboard, from across the room or across the internet.

How it works
1. Install Tetramote on your Mac, Windows or Linux computer from tetramote.com. It sits in the menu bar or system tray.
2. Scan the code it shows, or paste its link.
3. Connect again any time without a code. Your phone and computer connect directly when they can, on the same Wi-Fi or across the internet.

What you can do
• Watch the computer's screen live, with its sound.
• Use the trackpad under the screen: drag to move the pointer, tap to click, tap with two fingers to right-click and drag two fingers to scroll. Hold a finger still, then drag, to drag a window.
• Switch to direct touch and tap the screen itself, pinching to zoom in.
• Type on the phone's keyboard, with Esc, Tab, Command, Option, Control, Shift and the arrow keys in a row above it.
• Send your clipboard to the computer, or copy the computer's clipboard to your phone.
• Pick which display to show when the computer has more than one.
• Go full screen, with controls that float on top and hide after a few seconds.

Optimized for iPhone Duo
Folded, the computer's screen sits over a trackpad. Open it halfway like a laptop and the screen and the trackpad split at the fold.

Private
Sessions are end to end encrypted between your phone and your computer. The apps and the protocol are open source under the MIT license.

Tetramote needs the free Tetramote app on the computer you want to control.
promotionalText: See your computer's screen and use it with a trackpad and keyboard, from the couch or across the internet. Free and open source.
whatsNew:
• In trackpad mode, the pointer drawn on your phone matches the computer's pointer. It turns into an I-beam over text, arrows on a window's edge and a hand over links. Update Tetramote on your Mac or Windows computer to see it.
• A Bluetooth keyboard types through your phone's layout again, while shortcuts and arrows still go by position. To send every key by position, choose Raw in Settings.
• Zoomed in, the view follows the pointer as you move it, so it stays on screen.
